narratives.text: Users complete IdP login but the edge captive portal never receives release; IdP admin UI shows active sessions while network access stays blocked until manual portal refresh.
After LDAP WAN latency spike, authentication fails with bind timeout even though the IdP JVM process is healthy and local admin login works.
Sticky session lost after load-balancer failover; users forced through full login again while SSO cookie still present in browser.
Infinispan split-brain after network partition; different IdP nodes return conflicting login state for the same user.
SAML POST rejected at reverse proxy with 413; IdP assertion generation succeeds; bypassing proxy restores login.
SMS OTP arrives but verification step fails with expired state; password authentication already succeeded.
Migrating realm from IdP A to IdP B breaks audience claim mapping; same LDAP user authenticates on one stack only.
Concurrent OIDC callbacks from two tabs: second legitimate callback rejected as already used while first still pending.
Edge gateway accepts the same callback token twice under race; second network session granted without fresh IdP authentication.
Device cap policy counts rotating Wi-Fi MAC as new device each day; legitimate users hit quota.
SSO works when IdP and SP are co-located; fails across WAN with LDAP connection reset during user federation sync.
OIDC login loop: warm SSO session skips edge re-auth after ACL revoke; users appear signed in but packets dropped.
Keycloak cluster: login works on node 1 only; node 2 serves stale authorization codes from local cache.
HAProxy timeout truncates large SAML assertion before application ACS processes it.
Inter-site AD replication lag causes intermittent auth failure: bind succeeds locally, search returns empty on remote site.
Authorization server returns invalid_grant on PKCE mismatch; never reaches edge callback handler.
MFA push notification delivered but approving on phone does not complete web session; TOTP backup works.
Shibboleth SP logs successful IdP response but browser shows error at reverse proxy buffer limit.
Clock skew between RP and IdP invalidates assertion NotOnOrAfter during JWKS key rotation window.
Two IdPs share AD but issue tokens with different group claim format; app authorization fails after cutover.
WSO2 IS Hazelcast members list incomplete after VM restart; authentication state diverges between nodes.
Federated login to second IdP fails when primary IdP session still warm but edge session expired.
OTP SMS delayed beyond verifier timeout; users receive code too late to complete step.
SAML artifact resolution fails over high-latency link while HTTP-POST binding works in lab.
eduGAIN participant reports intermittent entity lookup failure during peak; SP-initiated flow times out at discovery.
Metadata refresh lag causes trusted partner login failure until federation aggregate updates.
Browser ITP drops third-party cookie on OIDC callback; IdP shows success while RP never receives state.
Redis session store failover leaves orphaned sessions; users see login page despite valid SSO cookie.
Cross-datacenter session replication exceeds TTL; user re-authenticates every few minutes.
Nonce replay detection fires on legitimate back-button navigation; false reject at token endpoint.

### Description Keycloak should forward passive authentication requests to SAML IDPs: 1. OIDC client sends authentication request with "prompt=none" parameter to Keycloak. 2. Keycloak forwards the **passive** authentication request to backing IDP This works if backing IDP is OIDC IDP (prompt=none is forwarded), but **does not work for SAML IDPs** Passive authentication in this context should be interpreted as: * "prompt=none" request parameter in OIDC * "IsPassive=true" attribute of AuthnRequest

## Description When a user authenticates at a higher Level of Authentication than a subsequent SAML SP requests during SSO re-entry, the token nulls out the classRef instead of asserting the requested URI. The root cause is an exact-equality check (token) at token — when the achieved level *exceeds* the requested level, the condition evaluates to token and clears the value, causing the SAML Response to carry token.
